title: Regional cost-prioritized fallback and tenant sharding reference
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page describes a reference architecture for multi-region VPC/private deployments that prioritizes cost-aware routing and graceful fallback while preserving tenant isolation, predictable SLAs, and fast recovery. It is intended for architects and SREs planning Redwood Private installs where customers run multiple regions and expect controlled cross-region fallback for capacity and cost reasons.

Goals
- Provide an operationally simple pattern to shift tenant traffic between regional model pools based on cost and capacity signals.
- Maintain tenant isolation and data residency constraints; only allow cross-region fallback when policy and contractual constraints permit.
- Minimize recovery time objective (RTO) for load surges while keeping incremental cost leakage visible and capped.
- Offer templates for shard placement, routing policy config, and safe rollbacks.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to Private (VPC) deployments using Redwood control plane with optional regional proxies.
- Assumes each region has at least one model pool (hot) and optionally a lower-cost, higher-latency cold pool (quantized/CPU-backed or smaller GPU class).
- Assumes tenancy model supports tenant metadata tags for residency and cost policy (e.g., residency=eu, fallback_allowed=true).
- Not a replacement for security or legal compliance reviews; consult security-and-compliance pages for data residency gating.

Architecture summary (text diagram)
- Regional control plane per-region (lightweight) -> Global orchestration layer (policy store, cost signals ingest) -> Regional proxies/local routers -> Model pools: hot-gpu, burst-gpu, cold-quantized.
- Failure / fallback flow described as: local hot pool exhausted -> regional proxy evaluates policy -> attempt cross-zone within region -> if unavailable, consult global orchestration -> select fallback region ordered by (policy, cost_score, latency_penalty) -> route via secure inter-region tunnel to fallback pool -> apply tenant isolation wrappers (encryption-in-transit, audit-tagging).

Key components and responsibilities
- Global Orchestrator (Policy Engine): Maintains ranked list of candidate fallback regions for each tenant, consumes telemetry (capacity, spot preempt probability, per-region unit cost), and produces routing decisions and constraints. Owned by: eng-platform.
- Regional Proxy / Router: Enforces local policy (no fallback if residency forbids), implements smart retries, and applies rate quotas. Owned by: eng-private-deployments.
- Model Pools: hot-gpu (SLO: p95 <= 120ms token latency), burst-gpu (SLO: p95 <= 200ms), cold-quantized (SLO: p95 best-effort <= 400ms). Owned by: eng-serving-runtime.
- Telemetry Sink / Cost Aggregator: Aggregates per-token cost estimates and emits cost_score. Owned by: eng-sre/finance.

Routing policy primitives
- residency_allowed: boolean (tenant tag) — if false, cross-region fallback is forbidden.
- max_cost_multipler: float (e.g., 1.5) — absolute cap on per-token cost increase relative to primary region.
- latency_penalty_threshold_ms: integer — maximum acceptable added latency before fallback disallowed.
- fallback_preference: ordered list of region candidates (explicit) or policy="cheapest" / "lowest-latency".

Operational runbook (for traffic surge or region outage)
1) Detection (automated): Regional proxy marks region-state=degraded when sustained p95 token latency > SLO by 25% for 3 minutes OR API error rate > 2% for 2 minutes.
2) Local mitigation: Regional proxy increases batching window (see batching guide), enables prefix cache sharing if available. If mitigation fails after 2 minutes, mark region-candidate for fallback.
3) Global orchestration: Query cost and policy store to determine allowed fallback targets. Produce ranked candidates where residency_allowed=true and cost_multiplier <= tenant.max_cost_multiplier.
4) Safe ramp: Route 1% of traffic to first fallback target for 60s while monitoring quality (latency, errors, generation quality metrics). If metrics stable, increase to 10% for 3m, then 50% for 5m, then full cutover. Abort and rollback on any step if error-rate or latency crosses abort thresholds (see SLO matrix).
5) Operator confirmation: If fallback crosses a contractual boundary (e.g., data residency change), operator approval required; orchestration will pause and create ticket.

SLOs and abort thresholds (recommended)
- p95 latency increase on fallback candidate: <= tenant.latency_penalty_threshold_ms (recommended 150ms).
- token error-rate: <= 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline.
- quality-regression: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity as defined by tenant eval set; abort if similarity drops by > 2 points.

Failure scenarios and playbook excerpts
- Scenario A: Primary region GPU fleet preempted (spot) causing sudden capacity drop. Playbook: Immediately mark affected pools degraded; orchestrator selects next cheapest non-preemptible region; initiate safe ramp; notify account owner and create incident with severity=high.
- Scenario B: Network partition preventing control plane updates. Playbook: Regional proxies operate on cached policy for up to 30m. If fallback needed, proxies use pre-approved local fallback list. Escalate to eng-sre after 15m.
- Scenario C: Cost spike in fallback region mid-ramp. Playbook: Telemetry sink will flag cost_multiplier breaches; orchestrator evaluates next candidate or initiates rollback; notify finance-affects.

Configuration examples
- Tenant metadata example (YAML):

  tenant_id: tenant-42
  tags:
    residency_allowed: "true"
    residency_regions: ["eu-west-1"]
    max_cost_multiplier: "1.3"
    fallback_policy: "cheapest"

- Orchestrator policy snippet (pseudo-JSON):

  {
    "tenant_selector": "tenant-42",
    "fallback_strategy": "rank_by(cost_score, latency_penalty)",
    "max_cost_multiplier": "1.3",
    "approval_required_on_residency_change": "true"
  }

(Operators should create entries via the policy UI/CLI; the orchestration will surface diff and require sign-off if approval_required_on_residency_change=true.)

Rollout checklist (table rendered as text)
- Preflight: verify telemetry collection and cost-aggregator sampling enabled across regions; verify tenant tags present (residency_allowed, max_cost_multiplier).
- Staging exercise: run simulated surge with shadow traffic to fallback region; verify safe ramp metrics and rollback logic.
- Legal check: confirm customer contract permits cross-region fallback for selected tenants.
- Communication: prepare email/sms templates for customer notification during cross-region activation.

Rollback and upgrade guidance
- Rolling back a regional fallback: the orchestrator supports reverse safe ramp with the same staged percentages but in reverse order. Always verify KV cache warmup before increasing traffic to primary.
- Software upgrades to proxies/orchestrator: use canary deploys that do not change policy semantics. For orchestrator schema changes, maintain backward-compatible migration path for 24 hours.

Monitoring and observability (required dashboards)
- Tenant-level dashboard: per-tenant token cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, fallback-region (label), current cost_multiplier.
- Region-level dashboard: GPU utilization, preempt probability, cold-pool queue-length, inter-region tunnel latency.
- Incident runbook hooks: automatic PagerDuty trigger when fallback abort threshold breached.

Security and compliance notes
- Any cross-region routing that moves customer requests to a different jurisdiction must include audit-trail tags and be logged to the evidence-blob for compliance.
- Encrypt inter-region tunnels with customer-linked keys where required by contractual KMS boundary.

Ownership and next steps
- Owners: eng-private-deployments (reference implementation), eng-sre (telemetry/costing), eng-serving-runtime (pool SLOs), legal (residency gating).
- Next steps: prototype in staged customer environment Q2-2026; capture results in /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-evacuation-simulation-safe-failover-playbook-2026.json.

References
- See: regional-proxy-fabric-and-data-path-segmentation (internal ref), vpc-tenant-commissioning-and-handoff-playbook (operator checklist), telemetry-ingest-aggregation-patterns-private-deploys (cost aggregator integration).

Appendix: quick CLI recipes
- Check eligible fallback candidates for tenant: redwoodctl fallback candidates --tenant tenant-42 --policy current
- Trigger a controlled 1% canary to region eu-west-2: redwoodctl route --tenant tenant-42 --to eu-west-2 --percent 1 --comment "canary-test"
